# Derivative description

Manufacturer facts of one MCU derivative, read-only for boards and projects: memory regions, peripheral instances and their clocks, pin multiplexing per package, clock limits, core, MPU and interrupt controller. One file per derivative under `mcudb/<family>/`, plus one generated pin multiplexing table per package.

Configuration level: **Derivative**. File: `mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml`, `mcudb/<family>/<part>.pinmux.yaml`. Schema: `Derivative`, `PinmuxTable` in [`tools/nxconfig/model.py`](../../tools/nxconfig/model.py).

254 fields in 44 objects. 0 fields have no description in the schema and 0 numeric fields have no unit; they are marked _missing in schema_ and _missing_. How to read the tables: [reference overview](README.md).

## Derivative file `mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml`

<a id="f-top-level"></a>

### (top level)

Derivative file `mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml`: manufacturer facts of one MCU derivative.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | integer |  | yes |  | `1` | Version of the file format; currently 1. |
| `derivative` | [object](#f-derivative) |  | yes |  |  | Identification, core and packages of the derivative. |
| `memory` | list of [object](#f-memory-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | Memory regions (flash, RAM, EEPROM window). |
| `instances` | map of string to [object](#f-instances-key) |  | yes |  |  | Peripheral instances; key: instance name as in the reference manual (e.g. `FlexCAN0`, `LPSPI1`), which boards use in `instance`. |
| `pinmux` | map of string to [object](#f-pinmux-key) |  | no | `{}` |  | Pin multiplexing per package; key: package name from `derivative.packages`. |
| `device_header` | [object](#f-device_header) |  | no | `null` |  | Vendor device header of the derivative. |
| `clock` | [object](#f-clock) |  | no | `null` |  | Clock facts: oscillators, PLL and frequency limits. |
| `mpu` | [object](#f-mpu) |  | no | `null` |  | Memory protection unit. Left out: no MPU described; code that needs it stops with an error. |
| `uid` | [object](#f-uid) |  | no | `null` |  | Unique chip identification. Left out: unknown; a project with a bootloader needs it. |
| `vim` | [object](#f-vim) |  | no | `null` |  | Vectored interrupt manager, VIM cores only. Left out: not described, no interrupt ranks possible. |
| `eeprom_emulation` | [object](#f-eeprom_emulation) |  | no | `null` |  | Codes of the one-time partition of the emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx FlexNVM). Left out: the derivative has no partitionable emulated EEPROM; a project with `nvm.partition` is rejected. |
| `pin_interrupts` | [object](#f-pin_interrupts) |  | no | `null` |  | Pins that can raise an interrupt on an edge, their lines and vectors. Left out: not described; a project with `pin_events` is rejected. |
| `comparators` | list of [object](#f-comparators-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | **After R1.** Analogue comparators with reference DAC whose output reaches a fault input of a PWM timer (hardware threshold). Empty: not described; a project with `hw_thresholds` is rejected. |
| `trigger_router` | [object](#f-trigger_router) |  | no | `null` |  | **After R1.** Trigger router between peripherals (PWM timer triggers to sample sequencers and fault inputs). Left out: not described; a project with `sample_groups` is rejected. |
| `sample_sequencers` | list of [object](#f-sample_sequencers-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | Sample sequencers that convert a list of channels on one ADC after one hardware trigger. Empty: not described; a project with `sample_groups` is rejected. |

### `derivative`

Identification and core of the derivative, packages and where its facts come from.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |

| `derivative.name` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Derivative name as the manufacturer writes it (e.g. `S32K144`); boards refer to it in `board.mcu`. |
| `derivative.family` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Family of the derivative (e.g. `s32k1xx`, `stm32`): selects the family clock model, the generators and the platform code. |
| `derivative.core` | string |  | yes |  |  | Processor core, a key of the core table of tools/nxconfig (e.g. `cortex-m4f`). |
| `derivative.fpu` | string |  | no | `null` | `none`, `sp`, `dp` | FPU variant: none, single precision (sp) or double precision (dp). Left out: the only variant the core has. |
| `derivative.nvic_priority_bits` | integer | bit | no | `null` | 2 to 8 | NVIC cores: number of implemented interrupt priority bits. |
| `derivative.features` | list of string |  | no | `[]` | item: `lmem_cache` | Optional core features: `lmem_cache` is the LMEM processor code cache (S32K14x), switched on at start-up. |
| `derivative.packages` | list of string |  | yes |  | at least 1 item | Package names of the derivative (e.g. `LQFP100`); `board.package` is one of them. |
| `derivative.pin_pattern` | string |  | yes |  |  | Regular expression of the pin names; every pin a board names must match it. |
| `derivative.sources` | list of string |  | no | `[]` |  | Documents and repository files the facts of this file come from. |
| `derivative.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: the entry as a whole is not confirmed by a source in the repository. |
| `derivative.example` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: format example only, not for real projects; using it gives a warning. |
| `derivative.jlink_device` | string |  | no | `null` |  | J-Link device name, if it differs from the derivative name. |
| `derivative.pyocd_target` | string |  | no | `null` |  | pyOCD target type, if it differs from the derivative name in lower case. |
| `derivative.openocd_target` | string |  | no | `null` |  | OpenOCD target script, e.g. `target/stm32f4x.cfg`. |

Decides which board and project entries may use the instance. |
| `instances.<key>.channels` | integer | none | no | `null` | > 0 | Timer: number of channels of the instance. GPIO port: number of pins of the port (their pin function is `GPIO` in the pin multiplexing table). |
| `instances.<key>.first_channel` | integer | none | no | `0` | ≥ 0 | Timer only: number of the first channel, 1 where the manufacturer counts from 1 (TIM1_CH1). |
| `instances.<key>.resolution_bits` | integer | bit | no | `null` | > 0 | ADC only: resolution of the converter. |
| `instances.<key>.channel_pattern` | string |  | no | `null` |  | ADC only: regular expression of the external channel names (e.g. `SE([0-9]\|1[0-5])`), checked against `adc[].channel` of the board. |
| `instances.<key>.internal_channels` | list of string |  | no | `[]` |  | ADC only: names of the inputs without pin (bandgap, reference, supply monitor) a project may use in `adc_internal`. |
| `instances.<key>.message_buffers` | integer | none | no | `null` | > 0 | CAN only: number of message buffers (mailboxes) of the instance. Left out: unknown. |
| `instances.<key>.clock` | [object](#f-instances-key-clock) |  | no | `null` |  | Functional clock of the instance. Left out: unknown; a project that uses the instance gets an error. |

<a id="f-instances-key-clock"></a>

### `instances.<key>.clock`

Functional clock of one peripheral instance (s32k1xx: clock gate of the PCC, fields PCCn.PCS/CGC).

Fact and decision are split (doc/architecture/README.md, section 4):

- the derivative names what the hardware allows - the selectable sources (`sources`), the asynchronous outputs the instance is wired to (`divider`) and the limit of the functional clock (`max_hz`), each with its source like every mcudb value,
- the project decides which of them is used (project.yaml peripheral_clocks.&lt;instance>),
- `default` is the choice that applies to a project which decides nothing. Without it an instance the project uses and does not choose a clock for is an error, so no value has to be invented for a derivative whose data sheet values are missing.

An instance without a clock select (`select` bus, core or none) has no `sources`: there is nothing to decide. Neither has an instance that runs on a named clock domain of the global clock module (`domain`, rm4x: VCLK, VCLK2, VCLKA1): its frequency follows from the domain the family clock model sets up.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instances.<key>.clock.sources` | list of string |  | no | `[]` | item: `SOSC`, `SIRC`, `FIRC`, `SPLL` | Clock sources the clock select of the instance offers. Empty for an instance without clock select (then `select` is set). |
| `instances.<key>.clock.divider` | list of integer |  | no | `[]` | item: `1`, `2` | Asynchronous outputs DIVx of the sources the instance is wired to (1: DIV1, 2: DIV2). |
| `instances.<key>.clock.default` | [object](#f-instances-key-clock-default) |  | no | `null` |  | Clock choice that applies when the project names none. Left out: a project that uses the instance must choose its clock in `peripheral_clocks`. |
| `instances.<key>.clock.max_hz` | integer | Hz | no | `null` | > 0 | Maximum functional clock of the instance (limit of the DIVx output) as the reference manual states it. Left out: no limit stated. |
| `instances.<key>.clock.select` | string |  | no | `null` | `bus`, `core`, `none` | For an instance without clock select: `bus` or `core` (runs on that clock), `none` (the clock is chosen inside the peripheral, e.g. s32k1xx FlexCAN CTRL1.CLKSRC). |
| `instances.<key>.clock.domain` | string |  | no | `null` | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | For an instance without clock select of its own that runs on a named clock domain of the global clock module (rm4x: `VCLK`, `VCLK2`, `VCLKA1`): the name of that domain, a key of `clock.max_hz`. Given alone, without `sources`, `select`, `divider`, `default` and `max_hz`. |
| `instances.<key>.clock.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `instances.<key>.clock.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `instances.<key>.clock.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-instances-key-clock-default"></a>

### `instances.<key>.clock.default`

One clock of a peripheral: source and the asynchronous output of that source it is wired to.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instances.<key>.clock.default.select` | string |  | yes |  | `SOSC`, `SIRC`, `FIRC`, `SPLL` | Clock source that feeds the instance (s32k1xx: SOSC, SIRC, FIRC or SPLL, the value of PCCn.PCS). |
| `instances.<key>.clock.default.divider` | integer |  | no | `null` | `1`, `2` | Asynchronous output of the source the clock is taken from: 1 for DIV1, 2 for DIV2. In a project entry it may be left out when the derivative allows only one output. |

<a id="f-clock"></a>

### `clock`

Clock facts of the derivative. Which source feeds what is the family clock model (tools/nxconfig/clock.py).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.internal` | map of string to integer | Hz | no | `{}` | key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`; value: > 0 | Frequency of each internal oscillator; key: its name (e.g. `FIRC: 48000000`). |
| `clock.oscillator` | [object](#f-clock-oscillator) |  | no | `null` |  | External oscillator input. Left out: the derivative has none. |
| `clock.pll` | [object](#f-clock-pll) |  | no | `null` |  | PLL limits. Left out: the derivative has no PLL. |
| `clock.lpo` | [object](#f-clock-lpo) |  | no | `null` |  | Frequency range of the low power oscillator that clocks the MCU watchdog. Left out: not described; a family whose watchdog runs on it (s32k1xx) cannot derive its safety timing then (error at `clock.lpo`). |
| `clock.max_hz` | map of string to integer | Hz | no | `{}` | key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`; value: > 0 | Maximum frequency per clock domain (`core`, `bus`, ...) in the run mode the drivers use. |
| `clock.system_source_max_hz` | map of string to [object](#f-clock-system_source_max_hz-key) |  | no | `{}` | key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Stricter domain maxima that apply only while a given source feeds the system clock (s32k14x: BUS_CLK 40 MHz with the SPLL as system clock). Key: system clock source of the family clock model. |
| `clock.output_max_hz` | [object](#f-clock-output_max_hz) |  | no | `null` |  | Maximum of every asynchronous clock output in the run mode the drivers use (s32k1xx: SPLLDIV1, FIRCDIV2, ...). The family clock model chooses the output dividers from it (the smallest divider within the limit). Left out: the outputs stay undivided. |
| `clock.pcc` | map of string to [object](#f-clock-pcc-key) |  | no | `{}` | key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Clock gates of peripherals that are not listed in `instances` because no generator configures them yet, but whose clock the clock driver switches on (s32k1xx: LPIT, LPTMR0). Key: name of the gate. |
| `clock.flash_wait_states` | [object](#f-clock-flash_wait_states) |  | no | `null` |  | Flash read wait states per band of the flash clock. Left out: not described (the flash needs none, or the family code does not configure them). |
| `clock.source_numbers` | [object](#f-clock-source_numbers) |  | no | `null` |  | Number of every clock source in the source select fields (rm4x GHVSRC). Needed by a family clock model with numbered sources (rm4x). Left out: the family has none. |
| `clock.external_max_hz` | [object](#f-clock-external_max_hz) |  | no | `null` |  | Maximum of every external clock input (rm4x `EXTCLKIN1`, `EXTCLKIN2`); keys are names of `source_numbers`. Left out: no external clock input described. |
| `clock.oscillator_monitor` | [object](#f-clock-oscillator_monitor) |  | no | `null` |  | Window of the oscillator clock monitor. Left out: no monitor described; the board's oscillator is only checked against `oscillator`. |
| `clock.domain_dividers` | map of string to [object](#f-clock-domain_dividers-key) |  | no | `{}` | key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | How each named clock domain is derived (rm4x: VCLK, VCLK2, VCLKA1, RTICLK); key: domain name, which is also its key in `max_hz`. Peripheral instances name their domain in `instances.<x>.clock.domain`. |
| `clock.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |

<a id="f-clock-pll"></a>

### `clock.pll`

PLL fed by the oscillator: output = oscillator / input_divider * multiplier / output_divider.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.pll.input_hz` | list of integer | Hz | yes |  | exactly 2 items; item: > 0 | [min, max] of the PLL reference after the input divider. |
| `clock.pll.vco_hz` | list of integer | Hz | yes |  | exactly 2 items; item: > 0 | [min, max] of the VCO frequency (reference * multiplier). |
| `clock.pll.input_divider` | list of integer | none | yes |  | exactly 2 items; item: > 0 | [min, max] of the input divider between oscillator and PLL reference. |
| `clock.pll.multiplier` | list of integer | none | yes |  | exactly 2 items; item: > 0 | [min, max] of the feedback multiplier. |
| `clock.pll.output_dividers` | list of integer | none | yes |  | at least 1 item; item: > 0 | Dividers between VCO and PLL output the hardware offers (s32k1xx: fixed 2). With `output_divider_stages`: every product of the stages, ascending. |
| `clock.pll.output_divider_stages` | list of list of integer | none | no | `[]` | item: exactly 2 items; item: item: > 0 | Output divider in stages, in signal order: [min, max] of each stage (rm4x: OD 1..8, then R 1..32). The PLL output is VCO / (product of the stages). Left out: one stage with the dividers of `output_dividers`. |
| `clock.pll.post_divider_input_max_hz` | integer | Hz | no | `null` | > 0 | Maximum of the clock between the first and the second output divider stage (rm4x: post-ODCLK = VCO / OD). Needs `output_divider_stages`. Left out: no limit stated. |
| `clock.pll.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.pll.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |

<a id="f-clock-lpo"></a>

### `clock.lpo`

Low power oscillator (LPO) of the derivative: always-on clock of the MCU watchdog and of other supervision timers (s32k1xx: the 128 kHz LPO of the PMC feeds the WDOG and, as LPO1K_CLK, the LPTMR of the period check). Timing that has to hold at every LPO of the data sheet (watchdog service interval, bounds of the period check) is derived from `min_hz` and `max_hz` by tools/nxconfig, never from the nominal value alone.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.lpo.nominal_hz` | integer | Hz | yes |  | > 0 | Typical frequency of the data sheet, the value the drivers load their counters for (s32k1xx: 128 kHz). |
| `clock.lpo.min_hz` | integer | Hz | yes |  | > 0 | Lowest frequency over process, voltage and temperature (data sheet minimum). |
| `clock.lpo.max_hz` | integer | Hz | yes |  | > 0 | Highest frequency over process, voltage and temperature (data sheet maximum). |
| `clock.lpo.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.lpo.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.lpo.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

Maximum frequencies of named clocks with their evidence (fact of the derivative).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.max_hz` | map of string to integer | Hz | yes |  | at least 1 character; key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`; value: > 0 | Maximum frequency per clock; key: clock or clock output name of the family clock model. |
| `clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-clock-flash_wait_states"></a>

### `clock.flash_wait_states`

Flash read wait states per band of the flash clock. The family code picks the band of the configured frequency and writes its values; how they are encoded in registers is family knowledge.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.flash_wait_states.clock` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Clock the bands refer to, a key of `clock.max_hz` (rm4x: `HCLK`). |
| `clock.flash_wait_states.bands` | list of [object](#f-clock-flash_wait_states-bands-list) |  | yes |  | at least 1 item | Bands in strictly ascending `max_hz`; the last one covers the maximum of `clock`. |
| `clock.flash_wait_states.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.flash_wait_states.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.flash_wait_states.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-clock-flash_wait_states-bands-list"></a>

### `clock.flash_wait_states.bands[]`

Flash read wait states that apply up to one frequency of the flash clock.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.flash_wait_states.bands[].max_hz` | integer | Hz | yes |  | > 0 | Highest frequency of the flash clock this band covers; the next band starts above it. |
| `clock.flash_wait_states.bands[].data` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Data (random read) wait states (rm4x: FRDCNTL.RWAIT, for the EEPROM emulation bank EEPROM_CONFIG.EWAIT). |
| `clock.flash_wait_states.bands[].address` | integer | none | no | `0` | ≥ 0 | Address setup wait states (rm4x: FRDCNTL.ASWSTEN). |
| `clock.flash_wait_states.bands[].pipeline` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: the flash pipeline mode is required in this band (rm4x: FRDCNTL.ENPIPE). |

<a id="f-clock-source_numbers"></a>

### `clock.source_numbers`

Number of every clock source in the source select fields of the clock module (rm4x: the value of GHVSRC, VCLKASRC and RCLKSRC and the bit in CSDISx). The family generator writes these numbers; the clock model uses the names.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.source_numbers.numbers` | map of string to integer | none | yes |  | at least 1 character; key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`; value: ≥ 0 | Source name -> number (rm4x: `OSCIN: 0`, `PLL1: 1`, `HFLPO: 5`). Numbers the document marks reserved are left out. |
| `clock.source_numbers.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.source_numbers.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.source_numbers.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

### `clock.external_max_hz`

Same keys as `clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>` ([table](#f-clock-system_source_max_hz-key)); the paths start with `clock.external_max_hz` instead of `clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>`.

<a id="f-clock-oscillator_monitor"></a>

### `clock.oscillator_monitor`

Clock monitor of the oscillator input: the oscillator counts as failed outside the window reference / factor &lt; f &lt; reference * factor (rm4x CLKDET: all domains fed by OSCIN switch to HFLPO).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.oscillator_monitor.reference` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Internal clock the monitor compares with, a key of `clock.internal` (rm4x: `HFLPO`). |
| `clock.oscillator_monitor.factor` | integer | none | yes |  | > 0 | Width of the window: the oscillator has to lie above reference / factor and below reference * factor (both limits excluded). |
| `clock.oscillator_monitor.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.oscillator_monitor.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.oscillator_monitor.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-clock-domain_dividers-key"></a>

### `clock.domain_dividers.<key>`

How a named clock domain is derived from its parent clock (rm4x: VCLK = HCLK / 1..16). The family clock model takes the smallest divider that keeps the domain within `clock.max_hz.<domain>`.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.parent` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Clock the domain is divided from: a system clock of the family model (rm4x `HCLK`), another key of `domain_dividers` or a clock source of `source_numbers`. Where the domain has a source select, the source the family model uses (its reset default). |
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.dividers` | list of integer | none | yes |  | at least 1 item; item: > 0 | Dividers between parent and domain, ascending; `[1]` for a domain that follows its parent undivided. |
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.multiple_of` | string |  | no | `null` | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | The frequency of the domain has to be an integer multiple of the frequency of this other domain (rm4x: VCLK2 of VCLK). Left out: no such rule. |
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source` | [object](#f-clock-domain_dividers-key-other_source) |  | no | `null` |  | Dividers and limit that apply only while the domain runs from a source other than `parent` (rm4x RTICLK: divider 1/2/4/8, at most VCLK/3; from VCLK the divider is bypassed). Left out: no other source described. |
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-clock-domain_dividers-key-other_source"></a>

### `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source`

Divider and limit of a clock domain while it runs from a source other than its `parent`.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source.dividers` | list of integer | none | yes |  | at least 1 item; item: > 0 | Dividers that apply to the other source, ascending (rm4x RTICLK: 1, 2, 4, 8). |
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source.max_of` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Clock whose fraction limits the domain from another source (rm4x RTICLK: `VCLK`). |
| `clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source.divisor` | integer | none | yes |  | > 0 | The domain from another source runs at most `max_of` / divisor (rm4x RTICLK: 3). |

<a id="f-mpu"></a>

### `mpu`

Memory protection unit of the derivative: how many region descriptors the hardware implements.

Which unit it is follows from the family (s32k1xx: NXP system MPU at the crossbar, no Arm core MPU), and so does the register encoding of the count (MPU_CESR[NRGD]); that knowledge belongs to the generator.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mpu.regions` | integer | none | yes |  | > 0 | Number of region descriptors the hardware implements (RGD[0] to RGD[regions-1]). |
| `mpu.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `mpu.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |

<a id="f-uid"></a>

### `uid`

Unique identification of the chip: the bootloader derives nothing from it itself, it reports it (DID 0xF18C) and the tester derives the device key of the chip from it (HMAC-SHA256 of the project's master key over these bytes). `size` bytes of memory mapped 32-bit words from `address`, read in address order, each word most significant byte first (s32k1xx: SIM_UIDH..SIM_UIDL, UID127..UID0; stm32: UID[31:0] first).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uid.address` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Address of the first 32-bit word of the UID. |
| `uid.size` | integer | byte | yes |  | 4 to 32 | Length of the UID, whole 32-bit words. |
| `uid.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `uid.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |

<a id="f-vim"></a>

### `vim`

Vectored interrupt manager of the derivative (core with interrupt controller `vim`).

The priority of a request is its channel number (0 highest). The project gives ranks as with an NVIC; checks.py turns them into a channel order over the channels that are not fixed. How many channels an instance needs and how the requests are moved to their channels is known only to the family generator.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vim.channels` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 2 | Number of VIM channels (channel 0 to channels-1). |
| `vim.fixed` | list of [object](#f-vim-fixed-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | Channels the hardware fixes to a request; they are never given to a ranked interrupt. |
| `vim.requests` | map of string to integer | none | no | `{}` | key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`; value: ≥ 0 | Default channel of every interrupt request (request name -> channel after reset). The family generator moves a request to the channel of its rank with the channel mapping (rm4x: CHANCTRL) and needs to know where each request starts. Key: request name as the family code uses it (e.g. `DCAN1_LEVEL0`). |
| `vim.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `vim.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |

<a id="f-vim-fixed-list"></a>

### `vim.fixed[]`

VIM channel whose request the hardware fixes (e.g. an FIQ-only channel); interrupt ranks never get it.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vim.fixed[].channel` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 0 | VIM channel number. |
| `vim.fixed[].request` | string |  | yes |  |  | What the channel serves, as the source document names it. |
| `vim.fixed[].kind` | string |  | yes |  | `irq`, `fiq` | Interrupt kind of the channel; `fiq` never calls the RTOS. |
| `vim.fixed[].note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-eeprom_emulation"></a>

### `eeprom_emulation`

Partition of the emulated EEPROM (NVM-07): the codes of the one-time partition command of the derivative.

The emulated EEPROM is read and written through the RAM window of kind `eeprom_ram` in `memory`; its backup and the data flash share the region of kind `data_flash`. `data_flash_bytes + backup_bytes` of every code is that region's size. What the project chooses is `nvm.partition` of project.yaml.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eeprom_emulation.sizes` | list of [object](#f-eeprom_emulation-sizes-list) |  | yes |  | at least 1 item | EEPROM sizes the command accepts. |
| `eeprom_emulation.partitions` | list of [object](#f-eeprom_emulation-partitions-list) |  | yes |  | at least 1 item | Splits of the partitionable flash the command accepts. |
| `eeprom_emulation.timing` | [object](#f-eeprom_emulation-timing) |  | no | `null` |  | Write times. Left out: the EEPROM driver keeps its own conservative time limit. |
| `eeprom_emulation.keys` | list of [object](#f-eeprom_emulation-keys-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | NVM-11: key space sizes of the security module the partition command accepts (s32k1xx CSEc: FCCOB1). Empty: the derivative has no key space; the project must not ask for one. |
| `eeprom_emulation.endurance` | list of [object](#f-eeprom_emulation-endurance-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | NVM-11: guaranteed writes per ratio of backup to EEPROM in use (data sheet). Empty: not stated. |
| `eeprom_emulation.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `eeprom_emulation.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |

<a id="f-eeprom_emulation-sizes-list"></a>

### `eeprom_emulation.sizes[]`

One EEPROM size the partition command accepts (s32k1xx: EEPROM data set size code, EEESIZE).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eeprom_emulation.sizes[].code` | integer | none | yes |  | 0 to 15 | Code of the size in the partition command (s32k1xx: FCCOB4[3:0]). |
| `eeprom_emulation.sizes[].eeprom_bytes` | integer | byte | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Bytes of emulated EEPROM the code gives (0: none). |

<a id="f-eeprom_emulation-partitions-list"></a>

### `eeprom_emulation.partitions[]`

One split of the partitionable flash the partition command accepts (s32k1xx: FlexNVM partition code, DEPART). Several codes may give the same split; the project then names the one it wants.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eeprom_emulation.partitions[].code` | integer | none | yes |  | 0 to 15 | Code of the split in the partition command (s32k1xx: FCCOB5[3:0]). |
| `eeprom_emulation.partitions[].data_flash_bytes` | integer | byte | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Bytes that stay data flash. |
| `eeprom_emulation.partitions[].backup_bytes` | integer | byte | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Bytes that back up the emulated EEPROM (EEPROM backup, not addressable any more). |

<a id="f-eeprom_emulation-timing"></a>

### `eeprom_emulation.timing`

Write times of the emulated EEPROM. The generator derives the time limit of one write from them (NVM-07: the limit of the EEPROM driver in time, not in polls).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eeprom_emulation.timing.backups` | list of [object](#f-eeprom_emulation-timing-backups-list) |  | yes |  | at least 1 item | Times per EEPROM backup size; a split without its own entry uses the next larger backup. |
| `eeprom_emulation.timing.first_write_factor` | integer | none | no | `1` | > 0 | Factor on the longest write for the first writes after a reset (s32k1xx data sheet: up to 2x for EEE clean-up). |
| `eeprom_emulation.timing.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `eeprom_emulation.timing.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |

<a id="f-eeprom_emulation-timing-backups-list"></a>

### `eeprom_emulation.timing.backups[]`

Longest write to the emulated EEPROM for one backup size (data sheet).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eeprom_emulation.timing.backups[].backup_bytes` | integer | byte | yes |  | > 0 | EEPROM backup size the time applies to. |
| `eeprom_emulation.timing.backups[].write_max_us` | integer | µs | yes |  | > 0 | Longest time of one 32-bit write to the emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx data sheet: teewr32b, max). |
| `eeprom_emulation.timing.backups[].partition_typ_ms` | integer | ms | no | `null` | > 0 | Typical time of the partition command (s32k1xx data sheet: tpgmpart). Left out: not stated. |

<a id="f-eeprom_emulation-keys-list"></a>

### `eeprom_emulation.keys[]`

NVM-11: one size of the key space of a hardware security module the partition command reserves in the emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx: CSEc key size, FCCOB1[1:0]). The bytes come off the end of the emulated EEPROM.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eeprom_emulation.keys[].code` | integer | none | yes |  | 0 to 255 | Code of the key space in the partition command (s32k1xx: FCCOB1). |
| `eeprom_emulation.keys[].slots` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Key slots reserved (0: none). |
| `eeprom_emulation.keys[].system_slots` | integer | none | no | `0` | ≥ 0 | Slots of these the module itself occupies once any slot is reserved (s32k1xx: MASTER_ECU_KEY, BOOT_MAC_KEY, BOOT_MAC). |
| `eeprom_emulation.keys[].eeprom_bytes` | integer | byte | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Bytes of emulated EEPROM the key space takes. |

<a id="f-eeprom_emulation-endurance-list"></a>

### `eeprom_emulation.endurance[]`

NVM-11: guaranteed writes of the emulated EEPROM at one ratio of EEPROM backup to the EEPROM in use (data sheet). Below the smallest ratio the data sheet states nothing.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eeprom_emulation.endurance[].ratio` | integer | none | yes |  | > 0 | EEPROM backup bytes per byte of emulated EEPROM in use. |
| `eeprom_emulation.endurance[].writes` | integer | none | yes |  | > 0 | Guaranteed writes at this ratio (data sheet, min). |

<a id="f-pin_interrupts"></a>

### `pin_interrupts`

Pins that can raise an interrupt on an edge, their lines and vectors (IO-51).

What the project decides (which input raises events, edge, debounce, rate limit, rank) is `pin_events` of project.yaml; nxconfig checks it against these facts: the pin must be reachable, pins that share a vector share its priority (same rank), and pins that need the same line exclude each other.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pin_interrupts.edges` | list of string |  | no | `["rising", "falling", "both"]` | item: `rising`, `falling`, `both` | Edges the edge detectors can react to: `rising`, `falling`, `both` (both edges at once). |
| `pin_interrupts.lines` | list of [object](#f-pin_interrupts-lines-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | Edge detectors that serve one pin at a time. Empty: every interrupt-capable pin has its own detector. |
| `pin_interrupts.vectors` | list of [object](#f-pin_interrupts-vectors-list) |  | yes |  | at least 1 item | Vectors the edges arrive at. |
| `pin_interrupts.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `pin_interrupts.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `pin_interrupts.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-pin_interrupts-lines-list"></a>

### `pin_interrupts.lines[]`

Edge detector that serves one pin at a time (stm32 EXTI line, s32k3xx SIUL2 EIRQ).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pin_interrupts.lines[].name` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Line name as the reference manual writes it (e.g. `EXTI3`, `EIRQ5`); vectors refer to it in `lines`. |
| `pin_interrupts.lines[].pins` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Regular expression of the pins the line can be connected to (e.g. `P[A-H]3`). Exactly one of `pins` and `signal`. |
| `pin_interrupts.lines[].signal` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Signal of the pin multiplexing table whose pins the line can be connected to (e.g. `EIRQ5`); the pins then depend on the package. Exactly one of `pins` and `signal`. |
| `pin_interrupts.lines[].note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-pin_interrupts-vectors-list"></a>

### `pin_interrupts.vectors[]`

Interrupt vector (NVIC) or request (VIM) that pin edges arrive at.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pin_interrupts.vectors[].name` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Vector name as the family code uses it: the interrupt of the device header without `_IRQn` on an NVIC core (e.g. `PORTC`, `EXTI9_5`), a key of `vim.requests` on a VIM core (e.g. `GIO_A`). |
| `pin_interrupts.vectors[].pins` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Regular expression of the pins with an edge detector of their own that end in this vector (e.g. `PTC([0-9]\|1[0-7])`). Exactly one of `pins` and `lines`. |
| `pin_interrupts.vectors[].lines` | list of string |  | no | `[]` | item: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Lines (`lines[].name`) that end in this vector. Exactly one of `pins` and `lines`. |
| `pin_interrupts.vectors[].note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-sample_sequencers-list"></a>

### `sample_sequencers[]`

Sample sequencer of one ADC (IO-62): converts a list of channels after one trigger (s32k1xx: PDB).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sample_sequencers[].name` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Sequencer instance as in the reference manual (e.g. `PDB0`). |
| `sample_sequencers[].adc` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | ADC instance (`instances`, class adc) whose conversions the sequencer starts. |
| `sample_sequencers[].trigger_target` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Router output (`trigger_router.targets[].name`) that starts the sequencer. |
| `sample_sequencers[].slots` | integer | none | yes |  | > 0 | Conversions one trigger can start on the ADC (s32k1xx: pre-triggers of PDB channel 0, each with its own ADC configuration and result register). |
| `sample_sequencers[].back_to_back` | boolean |  | yes |  |  | `true`: the end of one conversion starts the next one (s32k1xx: back-to-back mode), no delay has to be planned between them. |
| `sample_sequencers[].counter_bits` | integer | none | yes |  | > 0 | Width of the delay counter from the trigger to the first conversion. |
| `sample_sequencers[].clock` | string |  | yes |  | `core`, `bus` | Clock domain the delay counter runs on (s32k1xx: SYS_CLK = core clock). |
| `sample_sequencers[].start_clocks` | integer | none | yes |  | 0 to 255 | Clocks of the sequencer between the trigger (or the end of the previous conversion) and the start of a conversion, on top of the programmed delay. |
| `sample_sequencers[].source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Same as [`memory[].source`](#f-memory-list). |
| `sample_sequencers[].verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Same as [`memory[].verify`](#f-memory-list). |
| `sample_sequencers[].note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

## Pin multiplexing file `mcudb/<family>/<part>.pinmux.yaml`

<a id="f-pinmux-top-level"></a>

### (top level)

Generated pin multiplexing file of one part (mcudb/&lt;family>/&lt;part>.pinmux.yaml).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | integer |  | yes |  | `1` | Version of the file format; currently 1. |
| `part` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Part (derivative and package) the table describes. |
| `selector` | string |  | yes |  |  | Meaning of the numbers in the table, e.g. `PORT_PCR.MUX`. |
| `source` | string |  | yes |  |  | Source file the table was generated from, relative to `mcudb/`. |
| `signals` | map of string to map of string to integer or map of string to integer | none | yes |  | value: value: ≥ 0; value: value: key: pattern `^[a-z0-9_]+$`; value: value: value: ≥ 0 | Signal -> pin -> function selector. Signal names are `<instance>_<function>` (e.g. `FlexCAN0_RX`, `FTM0_CH3`) or `GPIO`; the selector is a register value (s32k1xx PORT_PCR.MUX, stm32 GPIOx_AFR) or, where one number is not enough, named register values. |
